# SK7002 — Cognitive complexity is over the threshold

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

How hard a member is to read, by Sonar's published definition: nesting-weighted, with no penalty for a `switch`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Maintainability |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.8 |

## Why

Cognitive complexity is the metric worth gating on, and it is the one SonarQube users actually miss. It differs from cyclomatic complexity in the two ways that matter: a `switch` over twenty cases costs one, because a reader takes it in at a glance, and a condition nested three deep costs four rather than one, because a reader has to hold three contexts to understand it. That makes it track the thing people mean by "this method is hard" rather than the thing that is easy to count. The implementation follows Sonar's specification — increments for each control-flow break, a nesting increment for each structure nested inside another, one increment per sequence of like binary operators, and increments for `goto`, recursion and each `catch` — so a number here is comparable to a number from SonarQube on the same code.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (a) {
    foreach (var x in xs) {
        if (b && c) {   // +1, +2 (nested), +3 (nested) and +1 for `&&`
            Use(x);
        }
    }
}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (!a) {
    return;
}

foreach (var x in xs) {
    if (!Matches(x)) {
        continue;
    }

    Use(x);
}
```

## When it does not fire

A metric rule has no false positives in the sense doc 16 § R3 means: it reports a measurement against a threshold, and the measurement is either right or a bug. What it can be is *useless* — a threshold low enough to fire on ordinary code teaches people to switch the category off, which is the same outcome by another route. The default is therefore set well above the corpus's p99 rather than at the textbook number, and the threshold is an .editorconfig option so a repository can tighten it deliberately. Generated code is excluded from the rule entirely; doc 07 § Metrics keeps it in the aggregate numbers, which is a separate surface. The default threshold is 15, which is Sonar's own and the number doc 09's `ci` gate names.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK7002.severity`
- `dotnet_code_quality.SK7002.threshold (default 15)`
